newsitem.title: USA: Paracelsus restates results back to 1991.
newsitem.headline: Paracelsus restates results back to 1991.

text.p: Paracelsus Healthcare Corp said on Thursday it was restating results for the fiscal years from 1991 to 1995 and for the first three quarters of 1996, as a result of an internal inquiry by a special committee.

For the year ended September 30, 1991, net income was revised to $20.7 million from $14.9 million, in fiscal 1992, net income was revised to $10.4 million from $10.3 million and in fiscal 1993 it was restated to $6.9 million from $12.5 million, the company said. In fiscal 1994, net income was restated to $5.2 million from $11.8 million and in 1995, it was restated to $1.4 million from $13 million, the company said.

Paracelsus said results were restated because of accounting errors and irregularities in four areas -- receivables due from Medicare and other government programmes, the use of corporate reserves, provisions for bad debt expense relating mostly to two of the company's psychiatric hospitals in the Los Angeles area and deferral of facility closure costs, which affected only the 1996 quarterly information.

It said the restatements mostly affected the company's financial periods prior to its merger in August 1996 with Champion Healthcare Corp and before the merged company changed its fiscal year from September 30 to a calendar year. The company also said Ron Messenger had ceased to be chief executive, vice chairman and director of the company and a consulting relationship with former chief financial officer James Rush was terminated.
Paracelsus was not immediately available to comment further.
Paracelsus said it requested and received waivers of certain covenants under its senior bank credit agreement which were needed mostly due to the restatements.
The company said it had amended its credit agreement which provided adequate liquidity under more restrictive terms.
The performance of PHC Regional Medical Center in Salt Lake City was also very disappointing, Paracelsus said. It said options for the facility included a sale or closure.

Management has prepared the outline of a restructuring plan which would include a reorganisation, a reduction of corporate overhead, a focus on improving hospital margins, expanding a plan for divesting unprofitable and non-strategic operations and de-leveraging the balance sheet, it said.
Paracelsus said said it planned to implement a corporate compliance program and engage a financial advisor to assist it in exploring opportunities to maximise shareholder value.

The company said the special committee recommended the board adopt improvements to policies, procedures and internal controls and take other steps to prevent the recurrence of past accounting errors and irregularities.

Charles Miller, president, said: "Management's attention (over the past eight months) has been diverted from completing the merger assimilation process and implementing the operating improvement plan developed in conjunction with the merger."

He said: "Nevertheless, these events do not have any bearing on the sound fundamentals underlying the company's core hospital operations, which are the major determinants of the company's intrinsic value." Paracelsus was not immediately available to provide further details on the specific restatement of the first three quarters of the year ended December 31, 1996.
